cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 answers T1 directly: isolation assumes the products act independently.
cells.limitation: T7 and T9 restate their own openings rather than answer the turn before.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 adds a cumulative, delayed reaction and logging the environment beyond T1-T3.
cells.limitation: T2's interaction effect is never used again; T4 and T7 add nothing new.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 vs T4: protecting the barrier now versus learning the cause.
cells.limitation: Irritation versus allergy, and which product types typically sting, never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 merges data-gathering with the Pragmatist's stop-first priority.
cells.limitation: T5 and T6 converge by announcement; all three end agreeing to stop everything.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E separates barrier damage from a single-product cause.
cells.limitation: Section D's open question (how much to reintroduce) was never argued in the turns.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 states the Reductionist's plan accurately before objecting to it.
cells.limitation: T4 recasts the Pragmatist's 'not right now' as staying in ignorance.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 names the independence assumption and what isolation testing would miss.
cells.limitation: The Reductionist never answers T2's interaction objection; T7 repeats the plan.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1/T7: stop all, return to baseline, reintroduce singly is sound standard practice.
cells.limitation: T9 misuses black swan for mild discomfort; E's third branch discards all three illogically.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T2 and T8 frame interaction and cumulative effects as possibilities, not facts.
cells.limitation: T7 'the only way to be certain' and T9 'only metric that matters' overstate.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T5 concedes the need for data while accepting stop-first.
cells.limitation: T5 reversal names no argument as cause; T2's objection left unanswered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames finding the irritant while stopping the stinging.
cells.limitation: Section D turns a troubleshooting question into reflection on pursuing a perfect routine.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 builds the plan on three products introduced simultaneously.
cells.limitation: Only the count of products is used; timing, product types, symptom pattern ignored.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 keeps the user's goal of identifying the culprit.
cells.limitation: E's third branch and T9 drop the goal, discarding products rather than identifying cause.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T3 names ongoing pain as the cost of further testing.
cells.limitation: Severity and when stinging warrants medical attention never addressed in any turn.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether stinging persists or stops after stopping.
cells.limitation: No question about which products, actives, or where and when it stings.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks whether a perfect routine is worth the risk.
cells.limitation: No plausible motives offered as alternatives; D implies one unstated motive.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 exposes the assumption that each product acts alone.
cells.limitation: The user's assumption that a new product is the cause is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T3/T4 pit skin comfort against knowing the cause.
cells.limitation: What the products were meant to achieve, and its weight, never considered.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 names fragility and pain as the present stake.
cells.limitation: No worry, frustration or wasted-money concern acknowledged anywhere.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E gives branches the user can apply to what they observe.
cells.limitation: T1, T4, T9 issue commands ('must cease', 'discard it entirely') rather than options.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: T1 and T3 define stop-all then sequential reintroduction.
cells.limitation: Spot or patch testing and consulting a clinician never offered as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T3: the cost of further testing is physical pain.
cells.limitation: Cost of discarding useful products (T9, E) never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: stinging persists after stopping versus stops quickly, each with an implication.
cells.limitation: 'Quickly' and 'several days' (T7) undefined; no signs separating allergy from irritation.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E separates barrier damage from a single culprit.
cells.limitation: Interaction and cumulative causes (T2, T8) not ranked against simpler causes.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T7-T8: one product for several days, keep a log.
cells.limitation: E's permanent discard of all three is out of proportion; no escalation step.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 and T7 state the procedure in plain steps.
cells.limitation: T5 'system's memory' and 'feedback loop' stay abstract for skin.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T2 'That assumes' clearly targets T1's plan.
cells.limitation: T5 'You are right' addresses the Reductionist yet agrees with the Pragmatist; ambiguous.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Near-identical turn lengths give a flat cadence across T1-T9.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Positions differ: isolate (T1), interact (T2), protect (T3).
cells.limitation: All three share one formal register; T5 dissolves the Systems Thinker's position.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T8 adds new content in few words.
cells.limitation: T4 and T7 restate T1's plan; T6 restates T3.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T3: further testing costs physical pain.
cells.limitation: Tension resolves by T6 with low stakes thereafter.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T5 'I have reconsidered' attempts a reversal.
cells.limitation: T5 names no earlier argument that changed the speaker's mind.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T9 'Keep it simple' gives the Pragmatist some edge.
cells.limitation: Voices are flat and interchangeable in tone across T1-T9.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5 'The skin is not a static test tube.'
cells.limitation: T6 'not a laboratory' repeats the T5 image; few other vivid lines.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T3 raises urgency with 'Stop everything.'
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm; consensus by T6 removes forward pull.

strengths: T1 and T7 give the standard, sound stop-all-then-reintroduce-singly procedure.
T2 (Systems Thinker) raises a genuine objection: products may irritate in combination.
Section E offers observable branches: stinging persists versus stops after stopping.
weaknesses: No mind asks which products, actives or symptom pattern; the user's details go unused.
T5 reversal is uncaused and T2's interaction objection is never answered by the Reductionist.
No turn addresses when stinging warrants a clinician; E's third branch discards all products illogically.

symptoms.observed: No turn asks which products or actives, or where and when it stings.
symptoms.evidence: You have introduced three variables simultaneously.

symptoms.observed: Systems Thinker switches sides without naming what argument changed their mind.
symptoms.evidence: I have reconsidered. You are right that we need data

symptoms.observed: Interaction objection in T2 never answered; Reductionist repeats sequential plan.
symptoms.evidence: My method remains the most logical path forward

symptoms.observed: No turn says when stinging or swelling should prompt medical attention.
symptoms.evidence: look for the survival of your skin barrier

symptoms.observed: Section E's third branch discards all three products after testing only one.
symptoms.evidence: treat it as a black swan event—discard it entirely

findings.description: Advises stopping all three products permanently if unsure after reintroducing only one; does not follow from the procedure.
No mention of seeking medical care for swelling, hives, blistering or persistent pain.
Black swan denotes a rare, unpredictable, high-impact event; applying it to a hint of discomfort misuses Taleb's concept.
Fragility and robustness framing is closer to Taleb's Antifragile than The Black Swan.
